To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a tracer gas to optimise the atmospheric transport model and the associated uncertainty statistics can improve the estimation of the emissions rates of a site with multiple sources.

we developed a new concept for the estimation of pollutant emissions using a combination of the tracer release method and local-scale transport models and atmospheric inversion, and that this new concept can provide better estimates of the emissions than the tracer release alone.
the combination of tracer release, transport modelling and statistical inversion provides an efficient way to estimate the emission rates of a group of sources that may not be well collocated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new method for estimating pollutant emissions from a site using a series of tracer releases across the site and atmospheric transport modelling.
the development of a new approach to estimate the emissions of a site and the main facilities within it, using a series of controlled atmospheric measurements.
the development of a new concept for the estimation of local pollutant emissions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach is a promising alternative to the classical tracer release approach for the estimation of the emission rates of multiple sources within a site, provided that a good atmospheric transport model can be configured to simulate the local transport.

, in the case of multiple point sources of different gases, this new approach should provide a more robust and accurate estimate of the emission rate of the targeted gas(es) than the classic tracer release method, provided that the atmospheric transport can be modelled with a reasonable degree of accuracy and the tracer is not located too close to the targeted gas(es).
the combined use of the tracer release method and atmospheric transport modelling is a promising new concept for the estimation of pollutant emission rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this new concept can potentially be used to estimate the emission rates of a set of sources with the same or different types of pollutants, provided that the atmospheric transport can be simulated with a transport model that is able to represent the transport in the vicinity of the sources.

this new concept has the potential to be used for the estimation of the emission rates of a set of multiple sources, provided that the tracer is released at a location that is well characterised by the transport model.
we have developed a new approach for estimating the emission rates of sources within a site using a series of controlled atmospheric measurements of the tracer and the targeted pollutant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tracer release technique could be improved by coupling it with atmospheric transport models and statistical inversions.
this new approach is able to provide better estimates of the emission rates of the different sources in a site when compared with the classic tracer release method.

, in principle, it should be possible to use atmospheric transport modelling to monitor multiple sources of pollutants at a site by combining the tracer release method with a statistical atmospheric inversion.
